Problem description:
- There are n jobs processed on a single machine.

contexts.text: [BASELINE] Canonical task wording.

As a home baker using a single oven, decide the order to bake batches where each batch has an expected bake time, a promised pickup time, and an importance score, and aim to minimize the total penalty equal to each batch's importance multiplied by how late it finishes with zero penalty for on time batches, ensuring batches do not overlap in the oven.

As a freelance video editor with a sole workstation, schedule the clips for rendering where each clip has an estimated render duration, a desired delivery time, and a client priority, and arrange them to minimize the sum of priority times lateness while preventing simultaneous renders.

As a mechanic with a single service bay, sequence the repairs where each repair has a required service time, an agreed completion time, and a severity weight, and minimize the total weighted lateness cost with zero contribution for repairs finishing by their agreed time while the bay handles repairs sequentially without overlap.

As a hairdresser working from a single chair, plan the appointments given each style request's expected duration, requested end time, and customer importance, aiming to minimize the aggregate penalty calculated as importance multiplied by how long an appointment finishes after the requested time, while never double-booking the chair.

As a photocopy technician with a sole high speed printer, order the print jobs where each job has a print length, a promised pickup moment, and an urgency rating, aiming to keep the total sum of urgency times tardiness as small as possible and ensuring the printer processes jobs sequentially without overlap.

As a small clinic receptionist using a single examination room, arrange patient visits where each visit has a consultation length, an appointment time, and a clinical priority, and choose an order that minimizes the total of priority times minutes late with zero for on time visits, while the room hosts patients sequentially with no overlap.

As a cake decorator with a solitary decorating station, sequence the decorating tasks where each cake requires a setup duration, has a promised pickup slot, and a penalty weight for lateness, and schedule them to minimize the overall weighted late time while the station handles cakes sequentially without overlap.

As an IT operations engineer managing a single server, order maintenance jobs where each job has an execution length, a target completion moment, and an impact score, and minimize the total impact-weighted tardiness with jobs executed sequentially.

As a freelance tailor with a single sewing machine, plan the order of garment alterations where each alteration has an estimated sewing time, a customer deadline, and an importance factor, and find the sequence that minimizes the combined importance times lateness, ensuring the machine handles alterations sequentially.

As a mobile food vendor with a single grill, decide the sequence of meal preparations where each dish needs a cook time, has a promised pickup moment, and a customer priority score, aiming to minimize the sum of priority multiplied by how late dishes are served while never cooking overlapping items.

As a small photo lab with a single developing machine, schedule the print batches where each batch takes a processing duration, has a required ready time, and a client weight, and arrange them to minimize total weighted tardiness with zero contribution from batches finished by their required time and with no concurrent batches in the machine.

As a home renovation contractor with a single paint sprayer, order the rooms to be painted where each room needs a painting duration, has an agreed finish date, and a customer importance rating, and sequence them to minimize the total cost given by importance times lateness while the sprayer services rooms sequentially.

As a musician mastering tracks on a single mixing console, pick the order for tracks where each track requires mastering time, has a release deadline, and a priority weight, and minimize the total of priority multiplied by how late a track is completed with the console processing tracks sequentially.

As a florist using a single workbench, schedule bouquet assemblies where each bouquet takes assembly time, has a requested pickup hour, and a client urgency level, and choose an order to reduce the sum of urgency times minutes late while ensuring bouquets are assembled sequentially.

As a laboratory technician with a single centrifuge, arrange sample runs where each run has a spin time, an expected completion schedule, and a study weight, and plan them to minimize the total study-weighted tardiness with zero penalty for runs finished by their expected time and with no overlapping uses of the centrifuge.

As a content writer using a single laptop session, prioritize article drafts where each draft takes a writing duration, has a submission time, and an editorial weight, and order the work to minimize the sum of editorial weight times how late a draft is submitted while working on drafts sequentially.

As a dry cleaner operating a single pressing machine, sequence garments through pressing where each garment needs a press duration, has a promised pickup slot, and a customer penalty factor, and schedule them to minimize the total penalty equal to penalty factor times minutes late, ensuring the pressing machine handles garments sequentially.

As a small boat mechanic with a solitary hoist, schedule lifts where each lift takes a service duration, carries a required finish moment, and has an associated urgency weight, and arrange the sequence to minimize the aggregate urgency times lateness while the hoist serves boats sequentially.

As a single-stall car wash operator, order vehicle washes where each wash needs a service duration, has a customer promised pickup time, and a priority score, and find the schedule that minimizes the sum across cars of priority multiplied by minutes late with the wash bay used sequentially for cars.

As the head chef, plan the sequence in which meals use the single stove so that all plates are finished, and arrange them to keep the total of each dish's importance multiplied by how many minutes it is served after its promised time as small as possible, noting that no two dishes can cook at the same time and each dish must be cooked without interruption.

As the office assistant, decide the order to feed print tasks to the single copier to complete every document, with the aim of minimizing the total of document priority times how long each copy job finishes past its requested completion time, remembering that the copier handles only one job at a time and each print run must run to completion.

As the clinic scheduler, put patient scan appointments into an order on the single scanner so all scans are done, choosing the ordering that minimizes the sum of patient urgency weights times the amount each scan finishes after its scheduled time, and do not allow overlapping scans or splitting a scan once it starts.

As the delivery dispatcher using a single van that makes strictly back to back stops, sequence the package drop offs so all parcels are delivered, aiming to minimize the sum of recipient criticality values times the amount each delivery is late relative to its requested time, and ensure deliveries are done sequentially with no simultaneous drop offs.

As the factory planner, arrange the sequence for metal parts on the single milling machine so all parts are processed, with the objective of minimizing the sum of part priority weights times the extent each part is completed after its due date, while ensuring the machine works on one part at a time and each machining operation runs uninterrupted.

As the system administrator, queue batch programs on the single server so all tasks run, ordering them to minimize the total of task criticality multiplied by how long each job ends after its deadline, and operate so the server executes one batch at a time and each batch runs to finish without preemption.

As the librarian, schedule books to be scanned on the single scanner so all volumes get digitized, aiming to minimize the cumulative sum of collection importance times how many minutes a scan completes beyond its target time, while allowing only one book under the scanner at a time and scanning each book in one go.

As the electronics assembler, decide the order to run units through the single assembly station so all units are built, with the goal of minimizing the sum of product urgency weights times how late each unit is completed past its promised ship date, and keep the assembly station working on one unit at a time with no splitting of assembly steps.

As the gardener, plan the order to plant seedlings with the single rototiller so each plot is planted, arranging the sequence to minimize the total of plant importance values times how many days planting finishes after each preferred planting date, ensuring the tiller serves one plot at a time and each plot is completed in one pass.

As the bartender, choose the order to mix cocktails at the single bar rail so every drink is made, with the objective of minimizing the sum of guest priority multipliers times how late each drink is served relative to when it was requested, and allow the bartender to prepare only one drink at a time without pausing a preparation.

As the shoemaker, schedule shoe polishing tasks on the single bench so every pair is finished, selecting the order that minimizes the total of customer importance weights times how long a pair is completed after its promised pickup moment, and ensure only one pair is worked on at a time and the polish work is continuous until done.

As the tailor, decide the order to cut fabric pieces on the single cutting table so all pieces are produced, choosing the sequence that minimizes the aggregate of order priority weights times how much each piece is finished after its requested pickup time, with the cutting table handling one piece at a time and each cutting operation finishing uninterrupted.

As the printing press operator, sequence job runs on the single press so every print order is completed, with the goal of minimizing the total of client weightings times the duration each run ends after its promised delivery date, and make sure the press performs one run at a time without splitting a job.

As the repair shop foreman, order repair tasks for the single workstation so all items are fixed, aiming to minimize the sum of customer priority scores times how late each repair is completed beyond its quoted return time, and ensure the workstation handles one repair at a time and each repair continues until finished.

As the photographer, plan the order to edit photos on the single editing station so all galleries are ready, selecting the order that minimizes the sum of client importance values times how many hours each gallery is completed after its agreed delivery time, and schedule edits so the station works on one gallery at a time and each editing job is not split.

As the lab coordinator, schedule sample analyses on the single analyzer so every sample is processed, arranging the sequence to minimize the total of sample priority weights times the amount each analysis finishes after its deadline, and require that the analyzer runs one sample at a time and each analysis proceeds without interruption.

As the bakery manager, decide the order in which trays go into the single oven so that the total of each tray’s importance multiplied by how late it comes out after its promised pickup time is as small as possible, bearing in mind the oven can process only one tray at a time and every tray requires its own baking duration and pickup time.

As the garage foreperson, sequence repairs on the single vehicle lift so that the total of customer criticality weights times the lateness of vehicle handover is minimized, remembering the lift accepts only one car at a time and each repair has a defined work duration and expected return time.

As the laundromat attendant, queue the loads for the single industrial dryer to keep the sum of load priority times their tardiness relative to stated pickup times as low as possible, with the dryer operating on one load at a time and each load having its drying time and pickup slot.

As the café manager, decide the sequence of orders through the single espresso machine so the total of customer importance ratings times how late each drink is finished compared to its target pickup time is minimized, noting the machine extracts only one drink at a time and each drink takes a certain pull time and has a desired pickup moment.

As the makerspace coordinator, arrange the queue for the single three dimensional printer to minimize the total of project importance scores times the minutes of delay beyond each project’s requested completion, given the printer runs one job at a time and each print has a set run length and a desired finish time.

As the small cabinet shop owner, pick the order of cutting jobs on the single table saw to minimize the sum of job priority times lateness relative to promised delivery dates, keeping in mind the saw performs one cut job at a time and each job has a required machining time and a delivery date.

As the body shop manager, plan the sequence of paint jobs in the single spray booth so the aggregate of customer urgency weights times the lateness of vehicle pickup is minimized, with the booth accepting only one vehicle at a time and each paint task having a spray and cure duration and a promised pickup day.

As the machine shop supervisor, schedule the parts on the single CNC mill to minimize the total of part criticality multiplied by minutes finished after their target completion, noting the mill machines one part at a time and each part requires a known cutting time and a due date.

As the bicycle shop owner, order tune ups on the single repair stand to keep the sum of customer priority scores times the tardiness of completion as low as possible, remembering the stand holds one bicycle at a time and each service has an expected work duration and a requested return time.

As the small press operator, decide the order of bookbinding tasks on the single binding machine so that the overall sum of order importance multiplied by its lateness beyond the customer’s requested date is kept minimal, bearing in mind the machine binds only one book batch at a time and each batch has a binding time and a requested date.

As the film processor, plan the sequence of developing rolls through the single processing unit to minimize the sum of client priority values times how late each roll is ready past its requested pickup, with the processor handling one roll at a time and each roll needing a fixed processing duration and a pickup request.

As the small electronics repair shop owner, schedule device repairs on the single bench to minimize the aggregate of customer urgency weights times minutes of completion after the promised return time, noting the bench services one device at a time and each repair has an estimated repair length and a promised return time.

As the handyman scheduling repairs at a bench, decide the order to work on a set of repairs each with a required work duration, an expected completion target, and an urgency rating so that the aggregate of urgency times positive lateness is minimized and the bench processes only one repair at a time.

As the print shop supervisor, prioritize a queue of binding tasks on the single binding machine where each task has a processing duration, a promised delivery date, and a fine weight, and choose the order that minimizes the total of fine times lateness with the rule that the machine handles tasks sequentially.

As the workshop planner, arrange a set of parts on the single lathe where each part requires a machining time, has a due pickup time, and a client penalty weight, with the aim of minimizing total penalty weighted tardiness while the lathe processes parts sequentially.

As the laundry room attendant using the single dryer, order clothing batches that each take a drying time, have a requested ready time, and an importance score, so that the total importance times any tardiness is minimized and the dryer handles one batch at a time.

As the dentist managing appointments in a single chair, pick the order of patients where each appointment has an expected length, a planned appointment time, and a severity weight, aiming to minimize the total of severity times how late each patient is seen while the chair is used for one patient at a time.

As the catering lead working with a single oven, sequence trays where each tray requires a cooking duration, has an event time, and a guest weight so the overall sum of guest weight multiplied by tardiness is minimized and the oven accommodates only one tray at a time.

As the photo retoucher with a single workstation, prioritize a batch of edits where each edit takes a certain time, has a deadline for delivery, and carries a client weight, ordering them to minimize the overall sum of client weight times lateness while edits are done one at a time.

As the small brewery operator using a single fermenter, sequence small runs where each run needs a certain processing duration, has a target completion date, and a batch importance so that the sum of importance times tardiness is minimized and the fermenter handles runs sequentially.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of baking batches the home baker must run in the single oven. This is the count of batch entries to schedule.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each batch (e.g., order numbers or short labels) that will be scheduled in the oven.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier for a specific batch used to refer to that batch in the schedule and calculations.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Expected time (in minutes) the batch must occupy the oven to finish baking. Used to accumulate elapsed time and compute each batch's completion time.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: A numeric score representing how painful it is if this batch is picked up late. This weight multiplies the minutes of lateness to produce the batch's penalty.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The promised pickup time for the batch, expressed as minutes from the common start time. If a batch's completion time exceeds this value, the lateness (completion - promised_pickup_time_minutes) times importance_score contributes to the total penalty.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of video clips (jobs) that must be rendered on the single workstation.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each clip to be scheduled (each id refers to one render job).

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for this clip; matches one entry from the global clip_ids list.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Estimated render duration for the clip, in minutes; how long the workstation must run for this clip (used to compute completion times).

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Client priority for the clip (higher means more painful to deliver late); used as the multiplicative weight on minutes-late when computing the clip's penalty.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Requested delivery time for the clip, given as minutes from the common schedule start; completion after this time incurs tardiness (minutes late).

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of cars (repair jobs) waiting for service in the single bay; the count of jobs that must be scheduled.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list/array of identifiers for each repair job (one per car). These ids are used to reference the job-specific service time, promised completion time, and severity weight when building a schedule.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier for this specific repair job/car, matching one entry from repair_ids so you can link its attributes together.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Estimated time required (in minutes) for the bay to complete this car's repair. The bay handles repairs sequentially (one at a time) and service_time_minutes is non‑preemptive for computing completion times.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Seriousness rating for this repair: the per-minute penalty multiplier applied to any minutes the car finishes after its promised completion time (higher means more painful to be late).

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Agreed completion time for this repair (in the same minutes units as service_time_minutes). If the job's completion time exceeds this value, lateness = completion_time - promised_completion_time_minutes; otherwise lateness = 0.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of appointments (clients) the stylist must schedule on the single chair during the day.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each appointment/client to be scheduled; each identifier links to the appointment-specific fields below.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for this specific appointment/client (matches one entry in appointment_ids).

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Estimated time in minutes the stylist needs to complete this client's requested service; appointments cannot overlap and must be scheduled as contiguous blocks.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: A numeric importance weight representing how upset the customer will be if they finish late; used as the multiplier on minutes late when computing the penalty for this appointment.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The time the customer requested to finish by, expressed in minutes from the salon opening (or another consistent day-zero reference); finishing after this time incurs tardiness measured in minutes.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of print requests currently queued for the single printer. This is the count of distinct orders that must all be scheduled and completed.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list (or set) of the unique identifiers for each print request/order. Each identifier corresponds to one job entry with its pages, pickup deadline, and urgency.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier for this particular print order (matches one entry in order_ids).

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The print length for the order, expressed as number of pages (or an equivalent processing-time measure). This determines how long the single printer will be occupied by this order; processing is sequential and units must be consistent across orders.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The numeric urgency or importance of the order. This weight scales the penalty when the order is finished after its promised pickup time — higher values mean lateness is more costly.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The promised pickup time for the order. If the job's completion time exceeds this deadline, its lateness is (completion_time − pickup_deadline); if completed on or before this time, lateness is zero.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of patients in the morning that must be seen in the single exam room. This is the count of visits to schedule (integer).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list (or set) of unique patient identifiers (names or IDs). Each identifier links to one patient's consultation length, appointment time, and clinical priority.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier for this patient (matches an entry in patient_ids). Use this to refer to the patient's appointment, length, and priority when building the schedule.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How long the patient's visit takes, in minutes. This is the processing time on the single exam room and determines how long the room is occupied for that patient.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The patient's priority (a positive number) that measures how important it is they are not late. When a patient is late, minutes late are multiplied by this priority to compute their contribution to the total penalty.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The scheduled appointment time for the patient (expressed as a clock time or minutes from the clinic start). If the patient's finish time is after this time, lateness = finish_time - appointment_time; otherwise lateness = 0.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of cakes that must be decorated at the single decorating station. The scheduler must order all n_cakes; every cake will be processed exactly once.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of identifiers for the cakes to be scheduled (e.g., ['Cake1','Cake2']). Each identifier corresponds to one cake entry with its times and penalty.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this cake (the label used in the schedule and results).

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The time required, in minutes, to set up and fully decorate this cake on the station. Used to compute completion times when sequenced.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The penalty weight representing how costly each minute of lateness is for this cake. Multiply minutes late by this weight to get the cake's contribution to total cost.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The promised pickup time for this cake, given in minutes from the common schedule start. If the cake's completion time exceeds this minute, the difference is minutes late.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of maintenance jobs scheduled on the single server; indicates how many job entries are present and that each must be run exactly once in the sequence.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of identifiers for the maintenance jobs (IDs used to reference each job). This is the set of jobs to be ordered for execution; the list itself does not imply the execution order.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier (string or number) for this maintenance job used to reference it when specifying sequences and reporting penalties.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How long the job takes to run on the server, in the same time units as due dates (e.g., minutes). Execution times accumulate when jobs are sequenced and determine each job's completion time.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The per-unit penalty weight (impact score) for finishing this job late. If a job finishes after its target_completion_time, its tardiness (finish_time − target_completion_time) is multiplied by this impact_score to form that job's penalty.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The target completion moment (deadline) for this job, in the same units as execution_time. Positive difference between a job's completion time and this target is its tardiness used to compute weighted penalty.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of garment alterations waiting to be sewn this afternoon; the number of jobs the tailor must schedule on the single sewing machine.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of unique identifiers for each garment (e.g., customer name or order code) used to reference each alteration job in the schedule and job list.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for this specific garment alteration (must match one entry from the global garment_ids) used to label its schedule position and penalties.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Estimated time the tailor needs on the sewing machine to complete this alteration (same time units used for all jobs); jobs are performed sequentially so this adds to cumulative machine time.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Importance or upset-level for the customer of this garment: the multiplier applied to any minutes/days of lateness. Higher values mean finishing late is more costly for that customer.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The promised pickup day/time for this garment (deadline). If the garment's finish time exceeds this, lateness = finish_time - promised_pickup_time; otherwise lateness is zero.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of orders waiting at the single-grill stall; the number of dishes that must be scheduled (positive integer).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of identifiers for each order/dish. Each identifier links to that order's cook time, promised pickup minute, and priority score used for scheduling.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this specific order/customer; used to tie together the order's cook time, promised pickup, and priority.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Minutes of continuous grill time required to prepare the dish. While this cook time is in progress the grill is occupied and no other order can be cooked.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Priority number for the order indicating how costly each minute of being served late is; used as the multiplier when computing that order's tardiness penalty.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Promised pickup minute for the order. If the dish finishes after this minute it accrues lateness equal to (finish_time - promised_pickup_minute); otherwise lateness is zero.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of print batches dropped off at the studio that must each run exactly once on the single developing machine. This is the count of items to schedule.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for the batches (one id per batch). These are the labels you will order into a schedule for the single machine.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for this specific print batch (matches one entry from batch_ids). Use this to refer to the batch when describing the schedule.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How many minutes the developing machine takes to process this batch (the uninterrupted run time on the single machine).

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The importance or penalty multiplier for this client: each minute the batch finishes after its ready time contributes client_weight × minutes_late to the objective.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The requested ready time (due date) for the batch, given in the same time units (minutes). If the batch finishes at or before this time it incurs zero tardiness; any finish after this time yields lateness = finish_time − ready_time_minutes.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of rooms that must be painted with the single sprayer; equals the number of jobs to sequence.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each room (one per room) to be scheduled; preserves the index or label used to refer to each room's data.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a specific room (matches one entry from room_ids) used to reference that room's painting task.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required to paint the room (in the same time units used for due dates); the sprayer will be occupied for this duration when the room is scheduled.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Customer importance rating for the room; used as the multiplier for that room's lateness when computing total penalty (higher means delays are costlier).

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The deadline the customer expects the room to be finished by (in the same time units as painting_duration). If the room's completion time exceeds this, lateness = completion_time - agreed_finish_date contributes to the weighted cost.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of tracks that need mastering on the single mastering board. This is the count of items that must be scheduled (an integer).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list or set of identifiers for each track (e.g., names or numeric IDs). These labels are used to refer to tracks when specifying their mastering time, deadline, and importance.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a single track (same label as appears in track_ids). Used to specify which track the following fields apply to.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required (in minutes) for the mastering board to complete this track. Tracks run sequentially; a track's finish time equals the sum of its mastering time and the mastering times of all earlier scheduled tracks.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Priority weight for the track: the penalty multiplier (cost per minute) applied to any minutes the track finishes after its release deadline. Total penalty contribution = importance_per_minute × max(0, finish_time - release_deadline).

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Scheduled release deadline for the track, expressed in the same time units (minutes) measured from the schedule start (time 0). Lateness is finish_time - release_deadline_minutes, floored at zero for on-time or early completions.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of bouquet orders waiting to be assembled on the single workbench (the count of jobs to schedule).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Array or list of identifiers for each bouquet/order (keys that match the detailed job items and determine which bouquets must be scheduled).

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this bouquet/order (string or integer) used to reference the specific assembly task in the schedule.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Time in minutes required to assemble this bouquet on the single workbench (the processing time p_i). Bouquets are performed sequentially and this is the duration added to the current clock when the bouquet is processed.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Client urgency level for this bouquet (the weight w_i). It multiplies minutes late to produce the penalty: higher urgency means late minutes are more costly.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Requested pickup time for this bouquet expressed in minutes from the scheduling start (the due date d_i). If the bouquet finishes after this minute, minutes late = finish_time - pickup_time_minutes; otherwise lateness is zero.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of centrifuge runs (samples) to schedule. Integer count of jobs that must each be run once on the single centrifuge; determines the length of the schedule.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered set or list of identifiers for each sample run (e.g., numeric indices or labels). There should be exactly n_samples identifiers; each identifier links the global list to the per-job fields below.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for this specific sample/run matching one entry in sample_ids. Used to reference this run when building the centrifuge sequence.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Duration in minutes that this sample occupies the centrifuge when run (non‑negative). Completion times are computed by summing spin_time_minutes of preceding runs plus this run; no preemption and runs cannot overlap.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Importance weight for this sample/study. If the run finishes late, the lateness in minutes is multiplied by study_weight to form the penalty; larger study_weight means being late is more costly.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Target (due) completion time in minutes from schedule start (time zero) for this sample. Lateness is max(0, actual_completion_time - target_completion_time_minutes); on-time or early finishes incur zero penalty.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of article drafts to write in this single laptop session (the count of jobs to schedule).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each article draft (one identifier per draft). These IDs are used to reference drafts when specifying their writing duration, submission time, and editorial importance.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier for this specific article draft (matches one entry from draft_ids); used to refer to this draft in the schedule and results.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Estimated time required to write the draft (time to complete the draft) measured in the same time units as submission times; used to compute the draft's finish time when ordering work sequentially.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Editor-assigned importance of the draft: the penalty multiplier per unit time of lateness. The draft's contribution to the objective is editorial_weight * max(0, finish_time - submission_time). Higher values make lateness more costly.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Target submission time (deadline) for the draft. If the draft is finished after this time, its lateness is finish_time - submission_time and is multiplied by the editorial_weight to compute penalty.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of garment orders waiting for the single pressing machine this morning — i.e., the number of jobs that must be sequenced.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of identifiers for each garment/order to be processed; each identifier refers to one pressing job in the schedule.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for this specific garment/order (matches one entry from garment_ids) used to reference its times and penalty.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Continuous time in minutes the press must run to complete this garment. The machine must allocate this many minutes consecutively when the garment is processed.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Customer-specific cost in monetary units per minute of delay; if the garment finishes after its pickup time, each minute late incurs this cost.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Promised customer pickup appointment time, expressed in minutes from the schedule start; if the garment's completion time exceeds this, lateness = completion - pickup_time_minutes.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of boat lifts that must be performed with the single hoist. This is the count of distinct jobs to schedule; every lift must be run once in some order.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each boat lift (one entry per lift). These IDs label the jobs the hoist must perform and are used to specify lift details and sequence decisions.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for this specific boat lift, matching one entry from the global lift_ids list.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Time the hoist is occupied to complete this lift (service duration). When scheduled, each lift takes this continuous amount of time during which no other lift can run.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Urgency (penalty weight) for this lift that scales how costly lateness is. If the lift finishes after its required finish time, the lateness is multiplied by this urgency to compute its contribution to the total penalty.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Requested finish moment (deadline) for the lift. If the lift's actual finish time exceeds this moment, the positive difference is the lateness that gets multiplied by the lift's urgency.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of cars that must be washed (each car is one job to schedule sequentially in the single wash bay).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of identifiers for the cars (labels or job IDs). Each identifier corresponds to one wash operation that must be scheduled.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for this specific car/job (matches an entry in 'car_ids'), used to reference the vehicle and its associated data.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required to complete this car's wash, in minutes. When the car is processed it occupies the bay for this duration.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Customer priority for this car: the penalty multiplier applied per minute the car finishes after its promised pickup time. Larger values make lateness for this car more costly.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Promised pickup time for the car, expressed on the same time scale as wash durations (for example, minutes from the schedule start or absolute clock minutes). If the car's finish time exceeds this value, its lateness is finish_time - promised_pickup_time (minutes); if not, lateness is zero.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of dishes the head chef must schedule on the single stove (an integer count).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of all dish identifiers (job IDs or names) that must be cooked once; each entry matches a job_id in the job items.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier or name for the dish used to refer to it in the cooking order and schedule.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Continuous cooking time required on the stove for this dish, in minutes; the dish must occupy the stove for this many uninterrupted minutes.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How costly it is (per minute) for this dish to be served late; the scheduler multiplies this weight by the dish's minutes of lateness to get its penalty contribution.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The promised service time for the dish, given as a minute on the same time scale as cook_time_minutes; if the dish finishes after this minute, lateness = finish_time - promised_minute (otherwise lateness = 0).

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of print requests (documents) the assistant must schedule on the single copier; the schedule must include each request exactly once.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each print request (e.g., document names or request numbers) that the assistant will order for the copier.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for this specific print request (matches one entry from print_job_ids) used to track and order the document on the copier.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How many minutes the copier takes to complete this document once started; the copier is occupied for this entire duration and a job cannot be preempted.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The importance (pain) multiplier for this document: each minute the job finishes after its requested completion time incurs this many penalty units (used to compute weighted tardiness).

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The requested completion time (deadline) for this document, in the same time units (minutes) as print_duration_minutes and measured from the schedule start (time 0); if the job finishes after this time, lateness = finish_time - requested_completion_time, otherwise lateness = 0.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of patient scan appointments that must be scheduled on the single scanner today (integer). Every appointment must appear exactly once in the final order; this is used to validate the number of job entries.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers (IDs or labels) for each appointment in the instance. Each identifier corresponds to one patient/scan and must match a job_item entry; the scheduler will produce a permutation of these IDs as the scan order.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for this appointment (must match one entry from appointment_ids). Used to link the processing time, urgency weight, and scheduled time to a specific patient/scan.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Duration of this scan in minutes (positive number). Once started the scan must run straight through and cannot be split or overlapped. Completion times are computed by summing scan_duration_minutes of jobs earlier in the chosen order plus this job's duration.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Patient urgency weight (nonnegative number) that scales how costly each minute of lateness is for this appointment. The objective multiplies minutes late by this urgency weight when summing penalties across patients.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The appointment's scheduled (due) time expressed as minutes from the start of the scheduling horizon (e.g., clinic opening). Lateness for an appointment equals max(0, completion_time - scheduled_time_minutes), where completion_time is the cumulative finish time in the chosen order.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of delivery stops the single van must make on this route. Used to know how many deliveries to sequence.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each delivery stop (one per package). Each identifier refers to one required stop that must appear exactly once in the route order.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for this specific delivery stop, matching one entry from the global stop list; used to reference this stop's times, urgency, and position in the planned sequence.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The time the van requires to complete this stop once it begins it — interpreted as the travel time from the previous stop plus any on-site drop-off/service time. This value is the 'processing time' used when computing finish times in a sequence.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The recipient's criticality or urgency rating for this delivery. If the delivery finishes after the requested time, the weighted lateness contribution is urgency_weight × (finish_time − requested_delivery_time).

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The requested delivery time for this stop. If the van finishes the stop after this time, the positive difference counts as lateness; finishing on or before this time yields zero lateness.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of metal parts (jobs) that must be processed on the single milling machine; this determines how many job records the planner must sequence.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list or set of identifiers for each metal part to be scheduled on the mill; each identifier links to one job item with processing time, weight, and due date.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this metal part/job (matches an entry in part_ids); used to refer to the job when building the machine sequence.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Uninterrupted time required on the milling machine to complete this part; measured in the same time units as due_deadline (e.g., minutes).

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Positive weight reflecting how costly it is for this part to be completed late; the schedule's objective multiplies any tardiness by this weight.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Target completion time (deadline) for the part; if the part finishes after this time, tardiness = completion_time − due_deadline, otherwise tardiness = 0.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of batch programs queued on the single server that must be scheduled (positive integer).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each batch job awaiting execution; each identifier indexes the job-specific parameters below.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this batch job (matches an entry in batch_ids) used to reference the job in the schedule.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Processing time p_i: the uninterrupted runtime required for this batch on the single server (time units).

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Weight w_i: the cost rate (importance) per unit of tardiness for this batch; used to multiply any lateness when computing total penalty.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Due date d_i: the target completion time for this batch; tardiness is max(0, completion_time - deadline).

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of volumes that must be scanned on the single scanner (the count of scheduled scans).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifiers for each volume to be scanned (e.g., labels or indices used to refer to individual scans in the schedule).

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier for this volume/scan (matches an entry from the global book_ids list).

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How many minutes it takes to scan this volume in one uninterrupted run on the scanner (the job's processing time).

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The importance of the volume's collection; used as the multiplicative penalty per minute of lateness (higher means finishing late is more costly).

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The target minute by which the scan should be finished (time measured from the schedule start). If the scan finishes after this minute, tardiness is finish_time − target_completion_minute; otherwise tardiness is zero.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of electronic units in this batch that must be built on the single assembly station; the scheduler must sequence exactly this many units.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers (IDs) for each unit in the batch; each ID refers to one distinct unit to be scheduled once on the assembly station.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier for a specific unit (matches an entry from unit_ids) used to refer to that unit when defining its processing time, due date, and urgency.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The fixed amount of bench/assembly time (in the task's time units) required to complete this unit on the station; a unit must use this entire time contiguously and cannot be split.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The unit's urgency multiplier representing how painful lateness is; each time unit the unit finishes late incurs this weight times the lateness as penalty.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The promised ship date for the unit (in the same time units as assembly_time); if the unit's completion time exceeds this value, tardiness equals completion_time − promised_ship_date and contributes to the weighted penalty.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Number of garden beds (plots) to be planted with the rototiller — the total count of tasks to schedule.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of unique identifiers for each plot/bed that must be planted (used to reference each plot's time, preferred day, and importance).

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for a single plot/bed (matches an entry in the global plot_ids list).

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Number of days the rototiller must work on this plot in one continuous pass to finish planting that bed.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Importance value for the plot: how costly each day of late planting is for this bed. The penalty contribution equals this importance multiplied by days planted after the preferred day.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The gardener's preferred day by which the plot should be finished. If the plot's completion day is later than this, lateness is (completion_day - preferred_planting_day).

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of cocktail orders the bartender must make (the count of drink requests in the queue).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each cocktail order (each item corresponds to one drink the bartender must prepare).

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this specific cocktail order (used to refer to the drink in the schedule).

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How many minutes the bartender needs, uninterrupted, to prepare this cocktail from start to finish.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Importance multiplier for the guest who ordered this drink; each minute the drink is served late incurs this many penalty units.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The time (in minutes from a common start) when the guest expects the drink; finishing after this time produces lateness equal to (finish_time - requested_time).

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of shoe pairs that must be polished at the bench; the count of jobs the shoemaker must schedule.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each shoe-pair job (one entry per pair). Use these IDs to reference each pair's polish time, promised pickup moment, and importance.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this specific shoe-pair job (matches an entry in pair_ids).

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Continuous time (in minutes) required on the bench to polish this pair; once started the shoemaker works straight until this duration is complete and the bench is occupied for that interval.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Customer importance score (penalty weight). Each minute the pair finishes after its promised pickup multiplies by this weight to give the job's contribution to total weighted tardiness.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Promised pickup moment (time in minutes from the schedule start) when the customer expects the pair. If the pair completes later, tardiness = completion_time - promised_pickup_time; if on or before, tardiness = 0.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of fabric pieces that must be cut today. This tells the planner how many cutting jobs will be scheduled (one job per piece).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The set or list of unique identifiers for each fabric piece to be cut. These IDs label the job entries below and are used to reference pieces when building the cutting sequence.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier for this particular fabric piece; must match one of the entries in piece_ids and is used to label the job in the schedule.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The uninterrupted time required on the cutting table to produce this piece. This duration uses the same time units as the pickup times (e.g., minutes) and determines how long the machine is occupied when this piece is processed.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The priority (penalty) factor for this piece: each minute the piece finishes after its requested pickup time contributes priority_weight × minutes_late to the objective. Higher values mean delays are more costly.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The requested pickup time for the piece (its due date). If the piece finishes after this time, lateness = finish_time − requested_pickup_time; if it finishes on or before it, lateness = 0.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of print orders in the morning queue for the single press. Use this integer to know how many jobs must be sequenced (each must be run exactly once).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each print order waiting to be processed on the press. These IDs are used to reference each job's times, weight, and due date when building a schedule.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this print order (matches an entry in order_ids). Use this to refer to the job when specifying its runtime, weight, and due date and when producing the sequence.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Amount of time the press must run to complete this order (same time unit as due_date). Jobs are non-preemptive: this full duration is scheduled contiguously on the press to compute completion times.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Numeric importance of the order for tardiness penalties. If the job finishes after its due_date, multiply its lateness by this weight when summing the total weighted tardiness to be minimized.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The promised completion time for the order. If the job's completion time is later, lateness = completion_time - promised_delivery_time (otherwise lateness = 0). Use this with press_run_duration and sequencing to compute each job's tardiness.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of repair tasks the foreman must schedule on the single workstation. Indicates how many jobs appear in the instance.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each repair task to be scheduled (one entry per repair). These IDs link to the per-repair fields below.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for this specific repair task (matches one entry in repair_ids). Used to reference this job in the schedule and in calculations of completion and lateness.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Clock time required on the single workstation to complete this repair. Repairs are non-preemptive (once started they run to completion) and this duration is used to compute completion times.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Customer priority score (weight) that scales the penalty for finishing this repair late. The schedule objective multiplies this value by the job's tardiness to compute its contribution to total penalty.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Quoted return time (due date) promised to the customer for this repair. If the repair finishes after this time, tardiness = finish_time - quoted_return_time (otherwise tardiness = 0); the objective uses priority_score * tardiness.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of photo galleries that must be edited on the single editing station (integer).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each gallery (e.g., numeric or short labels) in the instance; each corresponds to one uninterrupted editing job.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for this specific gallery, matching one entry from gallery_ids; used to refer to the gallery when building the schedule.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How many hours it takes the editor to finish this gallery in one continuous session (positive number, in hours).

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The client importance value for this gallery: the penalty multiplier applied to any hours the gallery is completed after its promised delivery time.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The agreed delivery time for this gallery (time in hours on the same timeline as edit_hours); if the gallery finishes after this time, tardiness is finish_time - promised_delivery_time, otherwise zero.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of samples in this batch that the lab coordinator must schedule on the single analyzer. This equals the count of sample entries to be ordered and processed one at a time.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of identifiers for each sample in the batch (e.g., numeric or alphanumeric IDs). These IDs are used to reference individual sample records when building the processing sequence and computing completion times.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier for this sample (matches an entry in sample_ids). Use this to refer to the sample when specifying order or reporting its completion and lateness.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The uninterrupted time the analyzer needs to run this sample from start to finish (processing length). This is used to compute each sample's completion time in a given sequence.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The numeric priority (weight) of the sample indicating how costly it is to finish late. If a sample finishes after its deadline, its penalty contribution is priority_weight multiplied by the amount of lateness.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The target finish time for the sample. If the sample's completion time exceeds this deadline_time, the lateness is (completion_time - deadline_time) and contributes to the total weighted tardiness.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of trays (orders) the bakery must bake this morning. This is the count of items to schedule on the single oven; scheduling starts at time zero.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each tray/order (e.g., 1,2,3...). Each identifier corresponds to one tray with its own bake time, importance, and promised pickup time.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for this specific tray/order matching an entry in the global tray_ids list.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Time (in minutes) the tray requires in the oven to finish baking. The oven handles one tray at a time and baking is non-preemptive; a tray's finish time equals the sum of its bake time and all bake times of trays scheduled before it.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How painful it is for this tray to be late: a multiplier applied to the tray's minutes of tardiness. The objective is to minimize the sum over trays of (importance_weight × minutes_late).

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Promised pickup time for this tray expressed in minutes from the scheduling start (time zero when baking begins). If a tray finishes after this time, its lateness is finish_time − promised_pickup_time_minutes (otherwise lateness is zero).

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of vehicle repairs waiting for the single lift. This is the number of jobs the foreperson must sequence.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of identifiers for each repair job (e.g., job numbers or vehicle IDs). These labels identify each car to be scheduled on the lift.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for this specific repair job (matches an entry from repair_ids). Use this to refer to the vehicle when building the service order.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How long the repair takes on the lift, measured in minutes (processing time). The lift must be occupied for this full duration when that job is scheduled.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: A numeric importance factor for the customer; higher means delays are more costly. The solver multiplies this weight by minutes late to compute the job's penalty.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The promised or expected handover time for the vehicle, expressed as minutes from the schedule start (time zero). If the job finishes after this time, its lateness in minutes is used to compute penalty.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of dryer loads to schedule (integer). This is how many separate loads the attendant must place into the single dryer during the planning window.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of identifiers for each laundry load (e.g., L1, L2, ...). Each identifier refers to one load that must be scheduled on the dryer exactly once.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for a specific load, matching an entry in load_ids. Use this to reference the load when building the dryer sequence.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Drying time required for this load, in minutes. This is the time the dryer will be occupied when this load runs; completion_time = start_time + drying_time_minutes.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Priority (penalty rate) for the load, typically a positive number. If the load finishes late, each minute of tardiness incurs this many penalty units; total penalty for the load = priority_weight * tardiness_minutes.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Requested pickup time (due date) for the load, given in minutes from the schedule start. Tardiness is max(0, completion_time - pickup_time_minutes). On-time or early completion yields zero tardiness.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of drink orders (tickets) to schedule on the single espresso machine for this shift; used to know how many jobs must be sequenced.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of unique identifiers for each drink order (e.g., ticket numbers); each identifier corresponds to one job that must be scheduled exactly once.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier for this specific drink order (matches an entry in order_ids); used to refer to the ticket when building the sequence.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Time in minutes the espresso machine takes to make this drink (the processing duration for this order). Completion times are computed by summing these pull times in the chosen sequence.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Importance rating for the customer/order (a numeric weight). If the drink is finished late, the penalty equals customer_importance × minutes_late; no penalty if finished on time or early.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Target pickup time for the drink expressed in minutes from the scheduling start time (the desired completion time). Lateness is max(0, actual_completion_time − target_pickup_time_minutes).

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of print projects waiting for the single 3D printer; the number of items that must be scheduled (an integer).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each print project in the queue (one id per project) used to refer to projects throughout the schedule.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for this specific print project (matches one entry from the global project_ids list).

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How long this print takes on the printer, measured in minutes of continuous machine time required to complete the project.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The project's importance rating: number of penalty units incurred per minute the project finishes after its requested completion time (higher means being late is more costly).

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The desired completion time for the project, expressed as a minute mark on the same time basis as the schedule (e.g., minutes from schedule start = 0); lateness is max(0, actual_finish_minute - requested_finish_minute).

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of cutting orders currently waiting to be run on the single table saw. This is the count of jobs that must be scheduled, i.e., the number of rows in the job list.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of unique identifiers for each cutting order (one per job). These IDs match the job-level records and are used to refer to orders when specifying the sequence.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this specific cutting order (matches an entry in cutting_order_ids). Used to reference the order when describing schedule position, start/finish times, and lateness.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Machine time required on the table saw to complete this order (expressed in the same time units used for due dates, e.g., hours). The schedule advances by this amount when the job runs; jobs run sequentially, so completion time accumulates.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Relative importance (penalty multiplier) for being late on this order. If the job finishes after its promised due date, its tardiness (finish_time - due_date) is multiplied by this weight to compute its contribution to the total penalty. Larger values mean the shop should prioritize avoiding tardiness for that order.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The promised delivery time for this order (in the same time units as cutting_time). If the job's completion time is later than this value, the job's tardiness equals completion_time minus promised_due_date; otherwise tardiness is zero.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of vehicles waiting for painting that must be scheduled sequentially in the single spray booth.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers (IDs or names) for each vehicle/job to be scheduled in the spray booth in some order.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for this specific vehicle (matches one entry from the global vehicle_ids list).

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Total time required in the booth for this vehicle (spray + cure), measured in days; used to compute completion times when vehicles are sequenced.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Nonnegative weight representing how costly a late pickup is for this customer; lateness for the vehicle is multiplied by this weight when computing total penalty.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The promised pickup day (due date) for this vehicle; if the vehicle's completion day exceeds this value, lateness = completion_day - promised_pickup_day, otherwise lateness = 0.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of parts (jobs) that must be processed on the single CNC mill. This is the integer count of items to sequence; the schedule must include exactly these parts.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of part identifiers (job IDs) corresponding to the parts to be scheduled. Each identifier links to one detailed job record (cutting time, criticality, and target completion).

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for this part (must match an entry in part_ids). Used to refer to the part when building a processing sequence and reporting completion times.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required on the mill to cut this part, expressed in minutes. This is the non-preemptible processing duration the mill spends when this part is run.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Numeric criticality (penalty multiplier) for the part. If the part finishes late, each minute of lateness is multiplied by this weight to compute that part's contribution to the total penalty.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Target completion time (due date) for the part, given in the same time units as cutting_time_minutes (minutes from schedule start). If the part's actual finish time exceeds this value, lateness = finish_time - target_completion_time; otherwise lateness = 0.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of bikes (jobs) on the morning list that must be serviced on the single repair stand; an integer number of tasks to schedule.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The collection/list of job identifiers for the bikes (e.g., customer or bike IDs). Each identifier references one service task described in the job items.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this bike's service job (matches one entry from the global bike_ids list).

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Expected time the repair stand is occupied to complete this bike's tune-up, expressed in minutes (or the same time unit used for due dates).

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Priority score for the customer indicating how costly minutes of lateness are; the tardiness penalty contributed by this job equals customer_priority_score × minutes_late.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The customer's requested return time for the bike, given in the same time units as service_duration_minutes and measured from the schedule start (e.g., minutes after the shop opens). Finishing after this time causes tardiness.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of book orders (batches) waiting to be run on the single binding machine; the count of jobs to schedule.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of identifiers for each book order/batch; these IDs are used to refer to individual jobs when specifying their schedule and computing completion times.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier for this specific book order/batch, matching one entry from the global order_ids list.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The time the binding machine needs to complete this batch (processing time). Used to accumulate running time and determine each job's completion time in a sequence.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The order's lateness importance (how painful it is to be late). This weight multiplies the lateness (if any) to produce the job's contribution to the total penalty.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The customer-requested completion time/date for this order. If the job's completion time exceeds this requested_date, the positive difference is the job's lateness used in the weighted penalty.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
