global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of film rolls to be developed that day — the count of distinct jobs the single processor must handle (an integer).

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of identifiers for each film roll (e.g., customer name, ticket number, or roll code). This enumerates all rolls available to schedule; the given order is not the processing order unless the solver chooses it.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier for this specific film roll (matches one entry from the global roll_ids). Used to refer to the roll in the schedule and results.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How long the processor needs to develop this roll, expressed in minutes. The machine can process only one roll at a time and each roll's development occupies consecutive minutes equal to this value.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Customer priority for this roll: the multiplier applied to each minute the roll is completed after its requested pickup. A larger value means lateness for this customer is more costly.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The customer's requested pickup time (deadline) for this roll, expressed in minutes from the start of the scheduling horizon. Lateness for the roll equals max(0, completion_time - requested_pickup_time_minutes).

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of repair jobs (devices) dropped off — the count of separate repairs to schedule sequentially on the single bench.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of identifiers for each repair job (e.g., ticket or device labels). These IDs are the items you will put into a bench schedule order.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier for this specific device/repair job (matches an entry in the global device_ids list).

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Estimated time required to complete the repair on the bench, expressed in minutes. Each job requires this uninterrupted time and jobs cannot overlap.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Customer urgency weight (a numeric score) that multiplies each minute the job finishes after its promised return time to produce the job's tardiness penalty.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Promised return time (due date) for the device, given as minutes from the schedule start (or converted to minutes). If the job finishes after this time, lateness = completion_time - promised_return_time_minutes; otherwise lateness = 0.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of repairs waiting at the bench that must each be completed once; used to know how many jobs to schedule.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each repair (e.g., labels or indices) so each repair’s duration, target, and urgency can be referenced.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier for this repair entry (matches one element of repair_ids) used to refer to the repair when ordering tasks.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How long the bench takes to complete this repair (time units, e.g., minutes). This is the uninterrupted processing time required on the single bench.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How painful lateness is for this repair: the per-unit-time penalty (weight) multiplied by any positive minutes the repair finishes after its target.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The hoped-for completion time for this repair (same time units as repair_duration). If the actual finish time exceeds this target, the positive difference contributes to the weighted tardiness.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of binding tasks to schedule on the single binding machine — the count of jobs in today's queue that must each be processed once.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each binding task in the queue. Each identifier links to one job item with its duration, promised delivery date, and fine rate.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique label for this binding task (matches an entry in the global task_ids list) used to refer to the task when building the schedule and computing completion times.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required on the binding machine to complete this task (in the same time units used for due dates). This duration is added to the machine timeline when the task is scheduled and determines its completion time.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Monetary fine (penalty) charged per unit of time the task finishes late. The total penalty for a task equals fine_rate × max(0, completion_time − promised_due_time).

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The promised delivery time for the task. If the task's completion time exceeds this value, the task incurs lateness equal to completion_time − promised_due_time, which is multiplied by the fine_rate to compute its penalty.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of parts waiting to be machined on the single lathe. This is the count of jobs that must be scheduled sequentially.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list or set of identifiers for each part/job (each identifier corresponds to one part that needs machining). These IDs match the job-level entries below.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this part/job (matches an entry in the global part_ids list). Used to refer to the part when specifying its times, deadline, and penalty.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Time required on the lathe to machine this part, expressed in the same time units used for scheduling (e.g., minutes). The machine will spend this duration processing the part without interruption.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Penalty weight representing how costly each minute of tardiness is for this part's client. Total penalty for the part equals max(0, completion_time - pickup_due_time) multiplied by this weight.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Requested pickup deadline for the part. If the part's completion time on the lathe exceeds this time, the part is late and incurs a weighted penalty; if completion is on or before this time, lateness is zero.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of laundry batches that need to be run on the single dryer. An integer count equal to the number of job entries; tells the solver how many loads must be sequenced.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers (strings or integers) for each customer's batch. Each identifier corresponds to one load that has a drying time, a requested ready time, and an importance score.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for this particular laundry load, matching one entry in 'batch_ids'. Used to refer to the specific batch in the schedule and results.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How long (in minutes) this batch must occupy the dryer to complete. The dryer runs one batch at a time and a batch cannot be split or interrupted; this value is used to compute completion times.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How painful it is for this customer to receive their load late — a positive weight. The penalty for lateness is importance_score multiplied by minutes late, so larger values mean the solver should prioritize avoiding tardiness for that batch.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The time (in minutes from the scheduling start) the customer requested the batch to be ready. If the batch completes after this time, its lateness is (completion_time - requested_ready_time); if on or before, lateness is zero.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: total number of patient appointments to schedule in the single-chair clinic.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: ordered list of identifiers (labels or indices) for each patient appointment; these IDs reference the per-patient fields below.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: identifier for this patient appointment (must match one entry in patient_ids); used to refer to this patient when building the schedule.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: expected length of this patient's appointment in minutes — the time the single chair will be occupied for this patient.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: numeric weight expressing how important it is that this patient is seen on time; each minute the patient is seen after their scheduled time incurs this weight multiplied by the minutes late.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: the planned appointment start time for this patient, measured in minutes from the clinic's day start; if the patient's finish time exceeds this value, tardiness is finish_time - scheduled_start_minutes (otherwise tardiness is zero).

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of trays that must be baked in the single oven for the catering run.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered set or list of unique identifiers for each tray that needs scheduling on the oven.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this specific tray (should match one entry from tray_ids).

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Continuous oven time required to cook this tray, measured in minutes (the job's processing time).

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Importance weight representing how painful it is to deliver this tray late; used to multiply any minutes of tardiness for the tray.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Scheduled event time (deadline) for this tray measured in minutes from schedule start; a tray finishing after this time is late by (finish_time - event_time_minutes), otherwise lateness is zero.

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of photo edits (tasks) the retoucher must perform sequentially on the single workstation; defines how many items are in the batch.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered or unordered list of unique identifiers for each edit (e.g., job numbers or filenames) used to refer to individual tasks in the schedule.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The unique identifier for this specific edit; must match one entry from the global edit_ids list and is used to reference the task in the schedule and output.

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How many minutes the retoucher needs at the workstation to complete this edit (processing is non-preemptive and tasks cannot overlap).

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: A positive number representing how important it is to avoid lateness for this client; used as the per-minute penalty multiplier for any minutes the edit finishes after its deadline.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The deadline for this edit expressed as minutes from the common scheduling start time; if the edit finishes after this minute its tardiness is (finish_time - delivery_deadline_minutes).

global_fields.name: n_jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of small brewery runs (batches) that must be scheduled sequentially in the single fermenter.

global_fields.name: jobs
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list or set of identifiers for each batch/run to be scheduled on the fermenter.

job_item_fields.name: job_id
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this specific batch/run (used to refer to it when specifying sequence and results).

job_item_fields.name: processing_time
job_item_fields.scenario_description: How long the batch occupies the fermenter (processing duration). Units are the schedule's time units; runs cannot overlap.

job_item_fields.name: weight
job_item_fields.scenario_description: Importance or penalty rate for finishing this batch late: each unit of time the batch finishes after its target date is multiplied by this weight.

job_item_fields.name: due_date
job_item_fields.scenario_description: The target (desired) completion time for the batch on the schedule; if the batch finishes after this time it incurs tardiness (finish_time - due_date).
